To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
kinesin-1 motors catalyse microtubule polymerisation by binding to the microtubules and using their motor domains to generate force that pulls on the microtubular lattice.

the motor core of the kinesin 13 family of microtubular motor proteins is an intrinsic microtubule-depolymerizing enzyme and that this depolymerization is regulated in vivo by a combination of localisation mechanisms and post-translational modifications.
kinesin- 13 motors catalyse microtubule end depolymerisation and that they are involved in many aspects of cell division.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how kinesin-1 and kinesin-14 motors work.
the mechanism of kinesin motor-catalysed microtubule end depolymerisation, and with the localisation and regulation of this process in vivo.
understanding how kinesin- 13 motors are localised to specific microtubule populations and how they are regulated in different cell types and at different stages of the cell cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
kinesin-14 motors are involved in the regulation of microtubular dynamics and in the regulation of the mitotic spindle, but the exact mechanism of action remains to be clarified.
kinesin- 13 motors are highly versatile, dynamic microtubule regulators that are essential for the maintenance of microtubular homeostasis in all eukaryotic cells.
kinesin- 13s are a class of molecular motors that are able to bend microtubule subunits at the microtubules ends and that this bending is the basis of the microtubular disassembly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
kinesin-1 motors are the 'workhorses' of the cell, whereas kinesin-8 and kinesin-12 motors have more subtle roles.
kinesin-14s are the motor for microtubule growth whereas kinesin-8s are responsible for the shrinkage of microtubular structures.
we have identified a conserved mechanism for kinesins-13 to depolymerise microtubules, and that this depolymerisation mechanism can be modulated by a conserved sequence in kinesin-8 motors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kinesin motors are a diverse family of proteins that have a common core structure and a conserved mechanism for catalysing depolymerisation of microtubles.
kinesin- 13s are not just motors that catalyse depolymerisation, but that they are also highly regulated and versatile proteins that can be adapted to perform a wide variety of cellular functions.
the kinesin motor domain is a versatile tool that can catalyse a variety of different activities.
